questions.stem_text: A string-handling function has been developed. The pseudocode for this function is shown below. For the built-in functions list, refer to the Appendix on page 18. FUNCTION SSM(String1, String2 : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER DECLARE n, f, x, y : INTEGER n 0 f 0 REPEAT n n + 1 x n y 1 WHILE MID(String1, x, 1) = MID(String2, y, 1) IF y = LENGTH(String2) THEN f n ELSE x x + 1 y y + 1 ENDIF ENDWHILE UNTIL (n = LENGTH(String1)) OR (f <> 0) RETURN f ENDFUNCTION

questions.stem_text: The engine management system of a car includes an energy-saving facility. When certain conditions are met, this facility will automatically stop the engine. The system is to be software-based. It will include a subroutine, EnergySaver, which repeatedly takes data from sensors in the car. The subroutine decides whether or not to set the EngineStop value. The table of identifiers used by this subroutine is shown below.

letters.label: (a)
letters.full_text: Complete the identifier table below by stating the data types. Identifier Data type Description Accelerator pedal position Values: 0 to 100 in steps of 1 Accelerator .......................... Meaning: 0: none (not pressed) 100: maximum (fully pressed) Engine temperature in °C EngineTemp .......................... (-50 to +150 stored to 1 decimal place) Normal engine temperature in °C NormalTemp .......................... Whole number; typical value 90 Road speed of car (in km/hr) Speed .......................... Values: 0 to 200 in steps of 1 Value used to signal engine must be stopped Possible values: EngineStop .......................... TRUE: stop engine FALSE: run engine [5] The condition for stopping the engine is that all three of the following are true: • Accelerator is not pressed • Engine temperature is normal or above • Car speed is zero The initial design stage will produce a prototype of EnergySaver, with a user interface. The structured English for this is: 1. INPUT value for accelerator pedal position 2. INPUT value for engine temperature 3. INPUT value for normal engine temperature 4. INPUT value for car speed 5. EVALUATE engine stopping condition 6. IF stopping condition satisfied SET engine stop value to TRUE 7. IF stopping condition not satisfied SET engine stop value to FALSE 8. OUTPUT message indicating engine stop value

To be a valid password, a string must: • be longer than 6 characters • contain at least one lower case letter • contain at least one upper case letter • contain at least one non-alphabetic character. FUNCTION Check(InString : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN DECLARE Index : INTEGER DECLARE StrLen : INTEGER DECLARE NumUpper, NumLower : INTEGER DECLARE NumNonAlpha : INTEGER DECLARE NextChar : CHAR NumUpper 0 NumLower 0 NumNonAlpha 0 StrLen LENGTH(InString) IF StrLen < 7 THEN RETURN FALSE ELSE FOR Index 1 TO StrLen NextChar MID(InString, Index, 1) IF NextChar >= 'a' AND NextChar <= 'z' THEN NumLower NumLower + 1 ELSE IF NextChar > 'A' AND NextChar <= 'Z' THEN NumUpper NumUpper + 1 ELSE NumNonAlpha NumNonAlpha + 1 ENDIF ENDIF ENDFOR ENDIF IF (NumUpper >= 1) AND (NumLower >= 1) AND (NumNonAlpha >= 1) THEN RETURN TRUE ELSE RETURN FALSE ENDIF ENDFUNCTION Refer to the Appendix on page 21 for a list of built-in pseudocode functions and operators. letters.intro_text: The following pseudocode algorithm has been developed to check whether a string contains a valid password. To be a valid password, a string must: • be longer than five characters • contain at least one numeric digit • contain at least one upper case letter • contain at least one other character (not a numeric digit or an upper case letter). FUNCTION Check(InString : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN DECLARE Index : INTEGER DECLARE StrLen : INTEGER DECLARE NumUpper, NumDigit : INTEGER DECLARE NextChar : CHAR DECLARE NumOther : INTEGER NumUpper 0 NumDigit 0 StrLen LENGTH(InString) IF StrLen < 6 THEN RETURN FALSE ELSE FOR Index 1 TO StrLen - 1 // loop for each character NextChar MID(InString, Index, 1) IF NextChar >= '0' AND NextChar <= '9' THEN NumDigit NumDigit + 1 // count digits ELSE IF NextChar >= 'A' AND NextChar <= 'Z' THEN NumUpper NumUpper + 1 // count upper case ENDIF ENDIF ENDFOR ENDIF NumOther StrLen – (NumDigit – NumUpper) IF NumDigit >= 1 AND NumUpper >= 1 AND NumOther >= 1 THEN RETURN TRUE ELSE RETURN FALSE ENDIF ENDFUNCTION The pseudocode does not work under all circumstances. The function was dry run with the string "1234AP" and the following trace table was produced. The string is an invalid password, but the pseudocode returned the value TRUE. Trace StrLen Index NextChar NumUpper NumDigit NumOther table row 6 0 0 1 '1' 1 2 '2' 2 3 '3' 3 4 '4' 4 5 'A' 1 3
